feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence from iteration 0: the oval finishes 16 of 20 with rms_error 0.0105 and max_error 0.032, well inside the 0.06 m limit, while the s-bend (line_loss_events 1.2, 18 of 20 off track) and slalom (line_loss_events 1.9, 20 of 20 off track) show high line loss with low rms_error. The Integrator had no integration problems with the [2,1,0,-1,-2] weights, kp 4, kd 0.5 or base_speed 1.6: steering_oscillation stayed between 0.24 and 0.35 and there were no controller errors. So the limit looks like sensor coverage at tight bends, not steering. Next race: if line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall below about 0.5 and the finish rate rises, keep the 16 mm footprint and move on to lookahead. If line loss falls but the robot still leaves the track, reduce lookahead (y 0.06 to 0.04) to test whether the off-track exits come from late reaction. If line loss stays high with the 16 mm footprint, widen the sensor span rather than the footprint, since the robot is losing the tape at the edge of the array. The body_width field has no effect on the off-track limit below about 0.19 m, so do not change it.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom are still above about 0.5 with sensor_size 0.016, widen the sensor span: x = 0.032, 0.016, 0.0, -0.016, -0.032 at y 0.06, keeping sensor_size 0.016. Evidence: iteration 0 slalom had 1.9 line losses with rms_error only 0.027, so the tape is leaving the sensor array rather than the controller tracking poorly.

If line_loss_events fall but the robot still goes off track, set every sensor y to 0.04 (from 0.06) to test whether a shorter lookahead helps the robot react to bends. Evidence: iteration 0 s-bend had 18 of 20 off-track ends with max_error 0.061, close to the 0.06 limit, and steering_oscillation of 0.35 leaves some margin to test this.

If the robot holds the line with low error and no line loss on all three tracks, keep the geometry and try wheel_track 0.14 (from 0.12) to add turn authority at base_speed 1.6. Evidence: the baseline control_effort on the s-bend (10.2) is the highest of any track, which suggests the wheels are working hard to turn.
